target_customer: German tax and accounting firms (Steuerkanzleien) and their SME clients
problem: Accounting firms spend hours on manual bookings, receipt splitting and chasing missing documents, and staffing shortages limit how many clients they can take on.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to accounting firms, integrated with DATEV

founders.name: Tim Hermes
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built software for accountants at Taxfix and scaled it to multiple millions in ARR in under 12 months.

founders.name: Markus Jungnickel
education: University of Cambridge, Law and Business
Imperial College London, MSc Computing Science
founders.background_notes: Worked on launching new financial services at Trade Republic.

founders.name: Kilian Justus
founders.background_notes: Product manager at Taxfix for tax filing launches in Italy and France; employee number 1 at genova.ai.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting invoice data and posting bookings via DATEV interfaces needs LLM pipelines plus integration work with a closed German accounting ecosystem, which is standard engineering with some hard integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: The product sits on top of incumbent accounting software, so a DATEV integration and firm workflow adoption give some stickiness, but the underlying AI approach was widely copyable in 2024.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated source found showing what incumbents did after 2024. The company positions itself as a layer on top of DATEV rather than a replacement.

market_need_then: The YC launch post says customers turn away 5 to 10 new clients weekly because of staffing shortages, and a 40-person firm customer quoted saved hours each week on split receipts. No revenue figures are given.

branding.domain_note: Site is tabula.de and email domain is gotabular.de; the product was announced on YC as Tabular, so the name appears to have changed from Tabular to Tabula. The reason is not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional German copy, taglines such as 'Superkraefte fuer Buchhalter' and 'KI, die mitdenkt', formal Sie address.

brand_strength.rationale: A search found no press about the brand itself; the name collides with many unrelated software packages called tabula or tabular, which makes it hard to find.

outcome_analysis: Tabula is an active Summer 2024 company with no shutdown, acquisition or layoff news found. The founders came from Taxfix and Trade Republic and sell an AI bookkeeping layer to German tax firms, a niche with clear labor pain. Funding and traction are only visible through aggregators and job posts, so its trajectory cannot yet be judged.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: Seedtable and a YC hiring page snippet say a 4.7M seed from LocalGlobe in 2024-09, while CB Insights shows a 0.5M convertible note on 2024-08-28 (5.2M total, investors Y Combinator, Project A, Phoenix Court, Rerail) and VCBacked shows 0.5M pre-seed. I could not open a primary announcement, so no round is recorded. A job posting claims over 1,000 companies onboarded, which is a recruiting claim. Competitor search returned only undated or later vendors (mika, Klardaten, GFR.ai, Norman, FINOM from 2025), so the competitor list is empty.
